problem_text:
A logistics manager is selecting cargo containers to load onto a transport vessel. The available containers are:
* Container 1: volume 22 cubic meters, revenue 247 units
* Container 2: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue 282 units
* Container 3: volume 44 cubic meters, revenue 259 units
* Container 4: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue 216 units
* Container 5: volume 19 cubic meters, revenue 23 units
* Container 6: volume 16 cubic meters, revenue 192 units
* Container 7: volume 23 cubic meters, revenue 174 units
* Container 8: volume 11 cubic meters, revenue 224 units
* Container 9: volume 13 cubic meters, revenue 212 units
* Container 10: volume 4 cubic meters, revenue 24 units
* Container 11: volume 18 cubic meters, revenue 288 units
* Container 12: volume 14 cubic meters, revenue 163 units
* Container 13: volume 10 cubic meters, revenue 16 units
* Container 14: volume 47 cubic meters, revenue 215 units
* Container 15: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue 136 units
* Container 16: volume 2 cubic meters, revenue 30 units
* Container 17: volume 40 cubic meters, revenue 101 units
* Container 18: volume 48 cubic meters, revenue 241 units
* Container 19: volume 39 cubic meters, revenue 86 units
* Container 20: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue 178 units
* Container 21: volume 20 cubic meters, revenue 210 units
* Container 22: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue 49 units
* Container 23: volume 33 cubic meters, revenue 253 units
* Container 24: volume 15 cubic meters, revenue 147 units
* Container 25: volume 17 cubic meters, revenue 27 units
* Container 26: volume 24 cubic meters, revenue 162 units
* Container 27: volume 37 cubic meters, revenue 140 units

The vessel's cargo hold has a maximum capacity of 441 cubic meters. Determine which combination of containers should be loaded to maximize total revenue without exceeding this volume limit. Each container must be either fully loaded or left behind.
